title: The M4 selected SDK 27 requires Swift 6.4 while the installed Command Line Tools still provide Swift 6.3.3

evidence.note: The first divergence is an Evaluation broker fault. Its retained evaluator stderr says `Metal Executor selected SDK differs`; the candidate had already been generated and sealed, so 76,922 provider tokens were spent before the deterministic host mismatch surfaced.

A fresh current-source helper build selected MacOSX27.0.sdk, SDK 27.0, Build 26A425. build.stderr says the SDK Swift module was built with Swift 6.4 while the installed compiler is Swift 6.3.3 and explicitly requires a matching toolchain. No helper or Executor was produced.

observation: Executor v106 truthfully bound SDK 26.5/Build 25F70. The M4 now selects SDK 27.0/Build 26A425, while com.apple.pkg.CLTools_Executables reports 26.6 and `/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/swiftc` reports Swift 6.3.3. The host is therefore not merely different from v106; its selected SDK and compiler are internally incompatible. Exact admission and the fresh helper build both refuse. Manually selecting the older SDK, restoring modes or reusing the old helper would manufacture the state checked and would violate the target/toolchain boundary.
proposed_change: Install the already offered Command Line Tools for Xcode 27.0 so the selected SDK and Swift compiler are one coherent toolchain. Then build both helpers from current source, capture the live family9 host, release a successor Executor and run the complete prebuild-first matrix baseline gate before any provider call. No Compiler, IR, verifier or kernel change is justified.
verification_plan: After explicit authorization for the system toolchain update: verify Swift and SDK compatibility with a fresh helper build, capture a live host document, publish a current family9 Executor from latest main, and require all selected matrix baselines to compile/seal/ABI-check before provider qualification.
